question: Should OpenClaw add declarative `bindings[].match.content` routing with `stripMatch`, or should content-driven routing be owned by a pre-routing plugin hook instead?
rationale: Both directions add public routing/API surface and affect session ownership, message delivery, route caching, regex safety, and plugin trust boundaries; current source, docs, and related open PRs do not settle that product choice.

options.title: Resolve API Direction First
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers choose whether declarative binding config or a plugin hook is the canonical content-routing surface.

options.title: Approve Binding Matcher
options.body: Add validated `match.content` config with explicit precedence, safe matching rules, cache behavior, docs, generated schema updates, and `stripMatch` semantics.

options.title: Supersede With Plugin Hook
options.body: Close or narrow this issue only after a reviewed pre-routing hook lands and documentation explains how plugins replace binding-level content routing.

recommendation.title: Resolve API Direction First
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers choose whether declarative binding config or a plugin hook is the canonical content-routing surface.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest current routing/config review history and already supplied maintainer-facing product context on this issue.
